articles.title: College football Week 2 players to watch: How will Texas run game fare against Ohio State?
articles.summary: Can Texas avenge a 14-7 loss at Ohio State from a season ago?
articles.body:
After a Week 1 that included an improbable win thanks to an added second, a blowout in Baton Rouge that few saw coming and a power outage in Tallahassee, Week 2 of the 2026 college football season is here.

Richmond at NC State, 7 p.m. ET Friday (ESPNU/DIRECTV)

Will the Miami transfer tackle everything in sight again on Friday night? Aguirre posted 18 total tackles in the Wolfpack's loss to Virginia in Week Zero. Granted, many of those stops were by necessity as Virginia just kept running the ball at the Wolfpack. The Cavaliers rushed 57 times for 258 yards as QB Beau Pribula threw just 11 passes. NC State is a heavy favorite against the Spiders; Richmond assuredly won't have that run-pass ratio. But the opportunity is there for Aguirre to post a big tackle number again.

Rutgers at Boston College, 7:30 p.m. ET Friday (ESPN2/DIRECTV)

Duff was the lone bright spot for Rutgers in the Scarlet Knights' Week 1 loss to UMass. He had nine catches for 196 yards and three touchdowns. And Rutgers might need that type of production again in Week 2.

The loser of Friday night's game will be in the running for the title of worst power conference team in the country. Rutgers, perhaps understanding the magnitude of the moment, has already made a QB change. Dylan Lonergan started in Week 1. AJ Surace will get the start against Boston College. Lonergan threw two TDs to Duff, but he also threw three interceptions and had a fumble.

No. 6 Oregon at Oklahoma State, Noon ET Saturday (ESPN/DIRECTV)

It was not a seamless transition to Oklahoma State for Mestemaker and his former North Texas teammates who traveled up Interstate 35 to Stillwater. The Cowboys opened the season with a second consecutive loss to Tulsa, as the offense managed just 10 points.

After throwing for nearly 4,400 yards in 2025, Mestemaker was 29-of-49 passing for 241 yards with a touchdown and two interceptions. Now the Cowboys get an Oregon team that will be motivated after a close Week 1 win over Boise State. And the Ducks beat the Cowboys 69-3 last season.

Arizona State at No. 10 Texas A&M, Noon ET Saturday (ABC/DIRECTV)

The former Kentucky quarterback had a fantastic debut for the Sun Devils against Morgan State. Yes, ASU played an overmatched FCS opponent, but Boley was 21-of-27 for 387 yards and threw six touchdown passes.

Can he come close to replicating that performance against Texas A&M? If so, the Sun Devils have a chance to pull the upset as two-touchdown underdogs. Boley is already at 40% of his passing touchdown total from 2025 after he threw 15 touchdowns across 301 pass attempt for a Kentucky team that struggled offensively in Mark Stoops' final season.

Duke at Illinois, 3:30 p.m. ET Saturday (FS1/DIRECTV)

Sheppard is the nation's leading rusher among players who have played in just one game so far this season. He got 35 carries for 227 yards in the Blue Devils' 17-3 win over Tulane.

With QB Darian Mensah at Miami, the sophomore rusher will be the centerpiece of Duke's offense in 2026 after he grew into his role as the Blue Devils' featured back in 2025. After five carries in each of Duke's first three games in 2025, Sheppard had at least 12 carries in every game the rest of the season and had more than 20 rushes over Duke's final four games of the year.

Still, 35 carries is by far a career high. That workload won't be sustainable, but Sheppard should get over 250 carries in 2026.

Iowa State at No. 21 Iowa, 7:30 p.m. ET Saturday (NBC/DIRECTV)

Moulton was the Hawkeyes' leading rusher with 878 yards a season ago and is well on his way to eclipsing that mark in 2026. The junior rushed for 183 yards on just 11 carries in a 40-0 win over Northern Illinois. Moulton had TD runs of 37 and 50 yards in the first quarter as the Hawkeyes ran for 289 yards as a team.

Moulton scored just five touchdowns a season ago and should find the end zone with far more regularity in 2026. He could be in line for another multiple-touchdown game on Saturday night against an Iowa State team that's basically brand-new in 2026 after coach Matt Campbell's departure to Penn State.

Georgia Southern at Clemson, 7:30 p.m. ET Saturday (ACC Network/DIRECTV)

How much will we see of the Clemson freshman against Georgia Southern? After earning the backup job in fall camp, Reynolds saw playing time in the Tigers' Week 1 blowout loss to LSU. It didn't go well, though it also didn't go well for anyone associated with Clemson in Week 1.

Reynolds was 4-of-6 passing for 22 yards and was sacked three times in relief of Christopher Vizzina, who was 10-of-16 for 83 yards and threw an interception.

After losing to LSU in Week 1 a year ago, Clemson also played a Sun Belt opponent in Troy. And that game wasn't a blowout. The Tigers won 27-16. Vizzina looks set to start again in Week 2, but if Clemson's offense struggles again or the coaching staff decides that it's time to play for the future, Reynolds could end up being the guy.

Texas RBs Raleek Brown and Hollywood Smothers

No. 1 Ohio State at No. 4 Texas, 7:30 p.m. ET Saturday (ABC/DIRECTV)

It's the first great test of Texas' overhauled running back room. The Longhorns' lack of a consistent ground game was a bugaboo in 2025, and Brown (Arizona State) and Smothers (NC State) were brought in as part of Texas' big-dollar offensive remodel in the transfer portal.

The initial results were encouraging against Texas State. Smothers rushed 10 times for 70 yards, and while Brown averaged just over three yards a carry, he scored two touchdowns. If they can force Ohio State to worry about the run game, that will open up more space for receivers Ryan Wingo and Cam Coleman to stretch the secondary.

articles.title: Eva Olid exclusive: Manchester United Women head coach 'surprised' by manner of London City defeat
articles.summary: Man Utd head coach Eva Olid on London City defeat, facing 'the best' Chelsea in her second game and how she wants her team to improve; Watch Chelsea vs Man Utd live on Sky Sports Mix from 11.30am on Sunday, kick-off 12pm
articles.body:
Even with some difficult pre-season results and a summer of transition hinting at teething problems, her methods had been sufficiently implemented on the Carrington training pitches to be confident going into last Friday's curtain raiser at London City Lionesses.

Olid knew her first WSL game was going be a challenge against Michelle Kang's star-studded big spenders but the manner of their 2-1 defeat - and a 100th-minute consolation from their only shot on target - was not on the agenda.

"What I saw surprised me a little bit," she tells Sky Sports , ahead of an already crunch showdown with Chelsea on Sunday. "We lost the game by ourselves, we didn't do what we had to do.

"In the friendlies we had played, we were making good progression about what we needed. In our last pre-season match against Man City we could have scored goals, we created chances. Of course, in friendlies if you make a mistake, it's a friendly. Everyone is confident.

"There were still a lot of things to build in terms of style, but we felt ready to compete. But then we reached that first match and the things we were doing in pre-season, we stopped doing. The pressure of the competition affected us in that first 45 minutes. It was a big learning."

Those first-day nerves were picked up on by pundits, who questioned how well Olid's new players were adapting to her methods. She has already admitted United will need to strengthen in January to add players fit for the style she wants to implement, but she insists those already there can succeed, too.

"We work in small spaces a lot in Spain - one, two touch, but here the players are not used to it," she says. "Working this way will help the players feel comfortable under pressure.

"Natalia Arroyo said something similar the other day. I love the physicality here but I think if you have that, plus the technical ability, it will get the best results."

There was always likely to be a period of transition following five years under Marc Skinner. Despite his record of overachievement, momentum needs to be rebuilt after a sour ending to his reign, a four-game winless streak at the end of last season.

But Olid was always going to do things her own way, too. She "revolutionised" former club Hearts, in the words of one Scottish newspaper - culminating in a first ever Women's SPL title last summer - and though she starts from a stronger base at United, she was never going to lose that courage of conviction south of the border, nor be shaken by any early wobbles.

"It's not the first time it's happened to me, a game like that," she says. "You want to help the players - but you cannot go inside their minds.

"I have always had things difficult and I have had to work so hard - and so nothing scares me. If things are difficult, I push harder, that's who I am.

"I don't like things being easy... If that happens, I don't feel useful, you know? I like the big challenges.

"Everyone is aware that it's impossible to change everything in a few weeks, and play 100 per cent as we want. But it's not like we have all the time we want and everything is fine if you don't win games."

It is difficult to know exactly how much is expected of Olid in her debut season given Manchester United's public shift towards youth development, and a summer of limited spending despite the loss of Melvine Malard to Chelsea.

The head coach is well connected to those reforms and was hired in part because of her track record of improving players and investing in youth.

Even a month into her time at the club, Olid is already well involved in the academy set-up at Carrington - and can enjoy a close-up view of potential future first-teamers now the Women's U21 side have finally moved across to the training base.

"Everything starts from the academy," she says. "My work is with them too, not just the first team. We need to make sure when they come up to join us, they are ready. It's not just bringing players from the academy because we have to.

"Over the international break, we will have meetings with the academy staff to begin implementing things. There are already a lot of things which are done really well, it's just about focussing on things like playing in possession, the technical parts - it's so important."

While Manchester United may not need a revolution in quite the same way as a Hearts team Olid inherited when they were bottom of the Scottish Premier League, she is wasting no time attempting to mould the club to create another legacy as she did in Edinburgh. "There is one difference, everyone told me it rains even more!" she laughs.

The spectre of Chelsea and Arsenal in their next two games, both live on Sky Sports , presents a daunting challenge for a coach trying to change so much so quickly. But this is what she relishes.

"At the end of he day, you have to play everyone twice," she adds. "Playing against the best is going to make us the best too."

Watch Man Utd vs Chelsea live on Sky Sports Mix from 11.30am on Sunday, kick-off 12pm.

articles.title: Phil Parkinson: Wrexham boss says West Ham game among 'lowest points' of career
articles.summary: Manager Phil Parkinson is downbeat after Wrexham suffer their heaviest league defeat for more than 22 years at London Stadium.
articles.body:
Wrexham manager Phil Parkinson admitted the 6-0 thrashing by West Ham United was among the lowest points of his time at the club.

The visitors were outclassed by a rampant West Ham at London Stadium on Friday.

It was Wrexham's heaviest league defeat in 22 years, since losing by the same margin at Bournemouth in 2004.

Parkinson said everyone had to take ownership of the performance, including himself.

"We're going to make sure we have that accountability as individuals and as staff," Parkinson said.

"We'll respond and we've got to put the ingredients back in place very quickly to put in a better performance than we did.

"[This] is the first night where we looked like we had a soft centre when it really mattered most and we've got to rediscover that.

"Everyone thinks it's been a complete bed of roses since I've been here [but] we've had other days that have been really, really tough.

"We've had setbacks and each season I've been here we've had periods where it's not been going well and from the outside the team can look a little lost.

"And then we've rediscovered what we're all about as a side.

"We've got to find a way back and give ourselves a chance. We need to show more character and resilience."

Latest Wrexham news, analysis and fan views

Jarrod Bowen scored his sixth goal of the season to set West Ham on their way to an impressive win that sent them back to the Championship summit.

Joel Piroe, Konstantinos Mavropanos, Taty Castellanos, Mohamadou Kante and Manor Solomon were also all on target for the Hammers.

It was bitterly disappointing for Wrexham in front of the biggest crowd they have appeared before.

"We came up against an exceptional front line tonight," Parkinson added.

"But equally in that first half those two goals – those two moments – we could have dealt with so much better.

"To come to a place like this with a team full of confidence you've got to defend with a lot more resilience and more tenacity in key moments than we did tonight.

"In the first 25 minutes there wasn't a great deal in the game and we got in some great positions.

"But the very basics of defending came up short and if you know where you need to be in those moments teams like West Ham are going to punish you.

"Part of me respects they are a good team, but we played Chelsea and Nottingham Forest, Coventry in the National League and Sheffield United and given a better account of ourselves in those games than we did tonight."

articles.title: Loris Karius Germany call-up discussion heats up after another Bundesliga masterclass
articles.summary: Loris Karius refused to campaign publicly for a Germany call-up after producing another decisive performance for Schalke 04 in Friday evening’s 3-1 Bundeslig...
articles.body:
Loris Karius refused to campaign publicly for a Germany call-up after producing another decisive performance for Schalke 04 in Friday evening's 3-1 Bundesliga victory over Union Berlin . That hasn't stopped the talk from escalating.

One week after emerging as Schalke's clear hero in a goalless draw with Bayern Munich , Karius again supplied several crucial interventions as Miron Muslic's side secured their first Bundesliga victory since returning to the German top flight.

The 33-year-old was barely tested during a dominant Schalke first half at the Stadion An der Alten Försterei. That changed significantly after Adil Aouchiche doubled the visitors' advantage immediately following the restart. Union responded by pushing Schalke progressively deeper.

Karius first denied Andras Schäfer from approximately 13 meters in the 54th minute before Tom Rothe headed against the crossbar one minute later. The former Liverpool goalkeeper then produced one of his best saves of the evening when Rothe found space on the left and drove a low effort toward the far corner. Karius reacted quickly to get down and preserve Schalke's two-goal advantage.

Tim Skarke tested him again with a powerful effort from distance shortly after entering, but the former Union keeper remained equal to it. Eventually, Union broke through. Skarke converted from close range in the sixth minute of stoppage time to reduce the deficit to 2-1 and transform what had appeared a comfortable Schalke victory into a frantic finish.

Two minutes later, Karius delivered again. Skarke found himself with another opportunity from approximately six meters following a chaotic sequence inside the penalty area. This time, Karius blocked the attempt and prevented Union from completing the comeback. Schalke subsequently broke in the opposite direction, with Maximilian Wöber finishing off a counterattack in the 13th minute of added time to seal the 3-1 victory.

Karius delivers again after Bayern masterclass

Friday represented the continuation of an exceptional two-match sequence for Karius. Only six days earlier, the Schalke keeper had been the central figure in his side's 0-0 draw with reigning champions Bayern Munich . Longtime Germany No. 1 Manuel Neuer endorsed Karius as the Man of the Match in that encounter. Karius officially received the honor this week.

Against Bayern, Karius helped an almost entirely defensive Schalke performance survive 90 minutes against overwhelming possession and pressure. Against Union, the promoted side produced an excellent first half, carried a deserved lead into the interval and created enough opportunities to potentially settle matters much earlier.

When Schalke's defensive structure finally began to bend, their goalkeeper ensured it never completely broke.

Another former Union player returns to Köpenick

Karius also shared something with Schalke goalscorer Robin Gosens on Friday evening. Both were returning to a former club. Karius spent the 2020/21 season at Union on loan from Liverpool as he attempted to rebuild momentum following spells in England and Turkey.

His time in Köpenick proved relatively brief. Karius served primarily as understudy to Andreas Luthe and made only five competitive appearances for Union before returning to Liverpool at the end of the campaign.

There was nevertheless a neat piece of symmetry attached to Friday's return. Karius' first Bundesliga start for Union came in February 2021. The opponent was Schalke. More than five years later, Karius returned to the Alte Försterei wearing Royal Blue.

Loris Karius Germany discussion continues to grow

Two outstanding performances in the space of six days have inevitably begun generating discussion beyond Schalke. Karius was asked after Friday's victory whether Germany head coach Jürgen Klopp had already contacted him regarding a potential return to the German national team .

The two know one another particularly well. Karius played under Klopp at Liverpool and reached the 2018 Champions League final during his time on Merseyside. To date, Karius has still not represented his country at senior level.

"No, there hasn't been any contact yet," Karius told reporters. "I have neither realistic nor unrealistic expectations. I'm not thinking about it at the moment, to be honest. When others bring me into the conversation, it's a nice validation of my work. I just try to help my team on a weekly basis. I just keep going and work hard every day. Everything else either comes or it doesn't."

The national-team question followed Muslic into his post-match press conference as well.

One reporter framed the matter particularly forcefully.

"In what universe is it conceivable that Jürgen Klopp won't nominate Loris Karius for the next international break?"

Muslic declined the invitation to lobby Germany's head coach publicly.

"I think Germany has a fantastic national team head coach," the Schalke trainer replied. "And I'm completely relaxed about his ability to nominate the right people."

articles.title: 👊Kevin Viveros emerges as Falcao's heir in Colombia
articles.summary: Colombian striker Kevin Viveros is enjoying a rich vein of form in South American football. At 26, the Athletico Paranaense forward has established himself a...
articles.body:
Colombian striker Kevin Viveros is enjoying a rich vein of form in South American football. At 26, the Athletico Paranaense forward has established himself as the Brasileirão's top scorer after netting 17 goals in 24 matches, leading his team to third place in the tournament under Odair Hellmann.

The solution to Colombia's attacking crisis

Combining physical power, speed, and lethal finishing in the box, the striker is emerging as the answer Colombia's national team has been looking for. With no established out-and-out number nine since the Radamel Falcao era, Viveros looks set to complement the attack alongside Luis Díaz .

Looking ahead to the new international cycle and the quest for continental revenge at the 2028 Copa América, Viveros is shaping up to be the key figure in leading the generational transition of the Colombian national team .

articles.title: Zeeland West shuts out Canadian opponent by 'diving around out there'
articles.summary: The Dux opened the doubleheader at Zeeland Stadium with a convincing win to remain unbeaten.
articles.body:
Zeeland West football vs Huron Heights best photos

ZEELAND - Logan Nash didn't look very tired for a kid who rarely left the football field.

The Zeeland West senior, who is a defensive back and running back, was making tackles left and right with his teammates in a 24-0 win over Newmarket Huron Heights, a team from outside of Toronto.

"That's just how we play football," Nash said. "We're diving around out there jumping on piles. We're nuts."

Huron Heights runs a very similar offense to Zeeland West's Wing-T.

"It's just like playing the Unity boys; hard-tough nosed football," Nash said of conference rival Unity Christian.

The Dux (3-0) got touchdowns from Brandon Holman, Drew Albrecht and Kenny Howe.

Jeff Bolhouse, the Dux coach, was pleased with his defense.

"We work on playing with a lot of energy and running through the ball," he said. "We work on a lot of pursuit drills in practice where we have to chase the ball all over the field."

But it was no fun in the first and third quarters when the Dux almost never touched the ball. Huron Heights had the ball for the entire first quarter and got nothing out of it. They missed a 27-yard field goal.

"It's like what we do to other teams," Bolhouse said. "Give those guys credit. They are big, strong and well coached. The run the veer option (offense) and they just pound the ball. But we made 'em work and didn't give 'em any big plays."

Holman, a senior, scored on a 39-yard run with 8:50 to go in the second quarter. Kenny Howe caught a pass from Albrecht for the two-point conversion. Albrecht, the quarterback, scored on a 1-yard run with 5:09 to go in the second. Holman scored on run for the two-point conversion for a 16-0 lead at halftime.

Huron Heights again had the ball for almost the entire third quarter but had nothing to show for it.

Howe, a junior running back, scored on a 4-yard run with 6:18 left in the game. Howe then carried the ball again into the end zone for the 2-point conversion. It was his third touchdown of the season.

"Kenny's a great addition," Nash said. "He's really been a good football player so far. He gives us a lot of effort and we love that."

articles.body:
Things to watch this weekend in the Atlantic Coast Conference:

No. 18 Tennessee (1-0) at Georgia Tech (0-1), Saturday, 7 p.m. ET (ESPN)

The Yellow Jackets are coming off a narrow loss to Colorado that came when they gave up a final-minute touchdown and then had Aidan Birr's field goal for the win blocked. Georgia Tech faces a stiffer test against the Volunteers, who got a huge debut from touted freshman quarterback Faizon Brandon against Furman.

Georgia Tech hasn't had an 0-2 start since going 0-3 in 1989.

Wake Forest (1-0) at Purdue (1-0), Saturday, noon ET (FS1)

Lopez showed a command and comfort of Rob Ezell's offense in a reunion with his coordinator from a successful run at South Alabama in 2024. Lopez's presence offers intriguing upside with the trip to face the Boilermakers in Big Ten territory.

Duke (1-0) at Illinois (1-0), Saturday, 3:30 p.m. ET (FS1)

The second of two ACC-vs-Big Ten matchups comes with the Blue Devils and Fighting Illini meeting for the second straight year. Last year, Illinois took over after halftime to cruise past a mistake-prone Duke team that would go on to win the ACC championship.

The Blue Devils look very different going into this matchup. Intead of now-transferred quarterback Darian Mensah , the offense revolves around physical runner Nate Sheppard , who posted a national-best 227 yards in the opener against Tulane . The Blue Devils will need more from San Jose State transfer Walker Eget at QB after he looked unsettled in his Duke debut and return from a knee injury from last season.

Pittsburgh quarterback Mason Heintschel . The sophomore threw for a national-best 453 yards while setting an ACC record with seven touchdowns in the opener against Miami ( Ohio ). The Panthers host UCF of the Big 12 on Saturday.

Clemson QBs Christopher Vizzina and Tait Reynolds . The Tigers host Georgia Southern on Saturday after an opening-game blowout loss at No. 8 LSU . Vizzina won a camp battle for the starting job as a senior against Reynolds as the promising freshman. Vizzina completed 10 of 16 passes for 83 yards and a pick-six, while Reynolds completed 4 of 6 passes for 22 yards. Clemson's offense needs to regroup regardless of who plays the most.

The ACC enters Week 2 with a 1-5 record against teams from the other Power Four conferences. ... Syracuse didn't win a game after QB Steve Angeli went down to an Achilles injury last September, but he returned with 263 yards passing and three TDs last week against New Hampshire . The Orange hosts California on Saturday. ... N.C. State hosts Richmond on Friday after managing just 168 yards in a season-opening loss at now-No. 25 Virginia . That marks one of just six times that the Wolfpack failed to crack the 200-yard mark under 14th-year coach Dave Doeren, according to Sportradar. ... Virginia Tech hosts Old Dominion on Saturday after scoring 73 points in James Franklin's coaching debut against VMI . That marked the No. 2 total in program history , exceeded only by scoring 77 against Akron in October 1995. ... Florida State and Stanford have open weeks.

articles.standfirst: El español es el único que ha conquistado Champions y Mundial este año
articles.summary: El español es el único que ha conquistado Champions y Mundial este año
articles.body: Empieza la turra del Balón de Oro y los candidatos se van posicionando. Ya saben, Mbappé, Lamine y demás galácticos lanzan sus mensajes o a sus acólitos con el objetivo de llevarse un premio que reconoce el talento individual en el deporte colectivo por excelencia. Ahí quizá radica el primer fallo, el segundo es el de no valorar realmente los méritos para obtenerlo. Hace tiempo, conquistar el Mundial (léase Cannavaro) era mérito suficiente para ganarlo. Si a eso le añades la Champions, algo que muy pocos han podido lograr el mismo año, tú candidatura adquiría otra dimensión. Pues bien, este 2026 hay un futbolista que ha reunido los dos galardones máximos del año y que no aparece en ninguna candidatura. Se trata de Fabián Ruiz. El sevillano formó parte destacada de la sinfónica del PSG que volvió a ganar la orejona. Y en el Mundial, ya saben, derribó la puerta de la titularidad sacando del once a una estrella como Pedri para acabar siendo también vital en la segunda estrella. Con un poco de marketing y autobombo su nombre debería estar entre los favoritos. Luego, cuando se confirme que no toca balón dorado, nos acordaremos de la injusticia como que Xavi e Iniesta no se alzarán con el del 2010.

articles.title: En busca del abrazo Vini-Bernabéu
articles.standfirst: El Real Madrid recibe hoy al Rayo (21:00 h) con la reconciliación entre la grada y Vinicius como telón de fondo, tras los pitos de la última semana, y con la obligación de reengancharse a la victoria en Liga
articles.summary: El Real Madrid recibe hoy al Rayo (21:00 h) con la reconciliación entre la grada y Vinicius como telón de fondo, tras los pitos de la última semana, y con la obligación de reengancharse a la victoria en Liga
articles.body: Ha sido una semana de opiniones encontradas en el coliseo blanco. La derrota ante el Betis y la sufrida victoria frente a un Inter que llevaba una veintena de partidos sin perder polarizaron al madridismo, y buena parte de ese descontento recayó sobre Vinicius. El brasileño fue pitado por un sector del graderío pese a firmar un partido notable en lo defensivo, y en alguna acción se llevó la reprimenda en forma de silbido. Por eso, coser ese abrazo roto entre el Bernabéu y su 7 se erigió en el eje de la comparecencia de Mourinho en la previa del partido de hoy contra el Rayo. El luso, fiel a su nueva versión más diplomática, no entró a juzgar los pitos, pero dejó claro de qué lado está echando mano de un refrán de su tierra. "En Portugal hay un proverbio, y es que solo tiras piedras a los árboles que tienen fruto", explicó. "¿Qué ha hecho Vini aquí en los últimos años, cuántas Champions ha ganado? Es un árbol que tiene mucho fruto, y la gente tira piedras porque quiere frutos. Quieren lo mejor de Vinicius, y lo mejor va a llegar". Su mensaje, más que una defensa, fue una promesa. Mourinho augura que la mejor versión del brasileño es cuestión de tiempo, porque los números avalan su entrega aunque el acierto aún no acompañe. "Está un Vini que trabaja más que nunca. En una era de datos, está muy cerca de su velocidad máxima: ha batido su récord en balones recuperados y también en el tercio defensivo. Va a llegar ya", insistió, recurriendo a un precedente esperanzador: "Ante el Benfica acabó él solo con la eliminatoria. Ese Vinicius va a llegar". Tampoco esquivó las críticas a Mbappé, a quien blindó con el mismo proverbio y hasta con cierta sorna hacia los agoreros. "Tiene razón, un jugador con más de 40 goles no es nunca un problema para el equipo", zanjó, antes de reivindicar el sacrificio del francés con una imagen elocuente. "Lo vi tras el minuto 90, con diez jugadores, defendiendo como un animal por delante de un Cucurella que estaba muerto. Yo valoro esto de un modo increíble. Hay gente que sabe tanto de fútbol como yo que también lo ha visto y no lo dice". Ese fue, precisamente, el gran dardo de la tarde a quienes no terminan de estar satisfechos pese a los resultados. "Dicen que podríamos haber encajado tres o cuatro goles ante el Inter, pero no dicen que podríamos haber metido ocho", protestó. "¿No están contentos porque hemos ganado? Nosotros seguimos nuestro camino. Hemos sufrido y perdido juntos contra el Betis y contra la vida, y vamos a hacer todo lo posible para que la gente esté feliz". Preguntado por las rotaciones de cara al Rayo, el portugués se negó comprensiblemente a desvelar algo del once, pero admitió que habrá novedades a su manera, rehuyendo la palabra y sustituyéndola por un concepto más de su gusto. "Existe un espacio para nueva energía, piernas con mucha gasolina", explicó, en alusión a los futbolistas que no jugaron ante el Inter. Eso sí, con la mira puesta solo en el rival inmediato: "No pienso en los tres partidos, pienso en el de mañana. Es un partido que tenemos que ganar". La comparecencia, celebrada en el propio Bernabéu por el Gran Premio de España de Fórmula 1 que toma este fin de semana IFEMA-Valdebebas, cerró con una nota distendida. Mourinho reconoció haber madrugado más de lo habitual por el evento —"he perdido 45 minutos de sueño"— y confesó su tentación de acercarse el domingo al circuito, no sin dejar un retrato de sí mismo cargado de retranca. "Soy amigo de Domenicali y tengo entrada, pero soy ese tipo de bicho que, si no gano, no hay vida. Si estoy contento, a lo mejor me paso", bromeó, dejando claro que su único gran premio, este sábado, se disputa sobre el césped ante el Rayo.

Real Madrid-Rayo.

articles.title: Valverde cierra el círculo ante el Rayo
articles.standfirst: El uruguayo, hoy pieza clave para Mourinho, vuelve a medirse al equipo ante el que jugó su último partido como lateral, un episodio que abrió la primera crisis de la 'era Xabi'
articles.summary: El uruguayo, hoy pieza clave para Mourinho, vuelve a medirse al equipo ante el que jugó su último partido como lateral, un episodio que abrió la primera crisis de la 'era Xabi'
articles.body: Del desacuerdo a la calma, y con el Rayo en medio. Este sábado, Fede Valverde se reencuentra con el equipo ante el que disputó su último partido como lateral derecho con el Real Madrid. Aquel 1 de febrero de 2026 puso el punto final a un capítulo engorroso, el de un centrocampista reconvertido a la fuerza en defensa, que llegó a desatar la primera gran crisis del entonces técnico, Xabi Alonso. El origen de todo estuvo en la enfermería. Con Carvajal y Trent lesionados, el tolosarra encontró en Valverde la solución de emergencia para el lateral, un parche que el uruguayo aceptó a regañadientes hasta que la paciencia se le agotó. El estallido llegó en la previa del duelo de Champions ante el Kairat Almaty, cuando el charrúa se sinceró. "No nací para jugar de lateral, no crecí aprendiendo a jugar en esa posición. Fue por una emergencia que me tocó jugar ahí", reveló en rueda de prensa. Todo retumbó y la respuesta de Xabi no se hizo esperar. Al día siguiente, Valverde fue suplente, con Asencio ocupando el lateral, y todos los focos se posaron sobre su calentamiento. Con actitud fría y las manos a la espalda, el uruguayo dejó una imagen gélida en tierras kazajas, ya que ni siquiera salió a ejercer de relevo de nadie. Fue el único partido de Champions de toda la temporada que no disputó, en un curso en el que completó el resto, incluido aquel en el que firmó un hat-trick ante el City. Con la llegada de Arbeloa al banquillo en enero, sus minutos en el costado fueron menguando de forma progresiva, hasta aquel último encuentro como lateral ante el Rayo. En total fueron 16 partidos jugando en el carril. El episodio quedó archivado, pero la espina de haber jugado fuera de su sitio tardó en cicatrizar. Valverde había cumplido por lealtad al escudo, aunque nunca ocultó dónde se sentía futbolista. El panorama, con Mourinho, no puede ser más distinto. Un Rayo que ha variado más bien poco, pilla a Fede en su salsa. El uruguayo se ha convertido en una de las piezas clave del luso, titular indiscutible en todos los partidos del curso y devuelto a su hábitat natural en el centro del campo, con gol ante el Inter incluido. El técnico, además, lo ha arropado en más de una comparecencia, blindándolo como uno de los pilares sobre los que edifica su proyecto. Precisamente en la última rueda de prensa, Mourinho quiso zanjar cualquier duda sobre la convivencia entre Valverde y Tchouaméni, con quien el uruguayo protagonizó un rifirrafe la temporada pasada. "Ellos lo han hecho todo, yo nada. Si llego al vestuario sin saber nada, me parecen dos grandes amigos", explicó el luso. "Cuando llegué, y Tchouaméni volvió del Mundial, estaba atento por si tenía que intervenir y hacer de ministro de la paz, pero no he hecho nada. El mérito es todo de los jugadores". Así, lo que hace unos meses era motivo de crisis hoy es sinónimo de estabilidad. Valverde vuelve a verse las caras con el Rayo, pero desde un lugar bien distinto: el de un capitán reconciliado con su posición, respetado por su técnico y dueño de la medular. El círculo, ante el mismo rival que lo cerró, se completa de la mejor manera posible.

images.caption: Valverde, marcando gol ante el Inter.

articles.title: Ruben Dias: Manchester City captain says new signings are 'desperate to win'
articles.summary: Manchester City have brought in summer signings who are "desperate to win" and the whole squad is "buying into the idea" of new manager Enzo Maresca, says new captain Ruben Dias.
articles.body:
Manchester City have brought in summer signings who are "desperate to win" and the whole squad is "buying into the idea" of new manager Enzo Maresca, says new captain Ruben Dias.

City spent a Premier League record £458m during the recent transfer window, with incomings including midfield trio Enzo Fernandez, Elliot Anderson and Ayyoub Bouaddi.

But the club also recouped more than £300m in sales and lost the experience of players such as 2024 Ballon d'Or winner Rodri, former captain Bernardo Silva and England international John Stones.

Dias has been part of City's leadership group since joining from Benfica for £65m in 2020 and has now been handed the armband by Maresca.

"In terms of the role I have, it goes down to trying to be the best version of yourself, and in terms of that, nothing has changed," Dias told the Football Interview.

"So many people have left and so many winners have left, and now new people have joined with a lot of ambition and people that are desperate to win and that is also what makes the club keep on going.

"Others, Enzo included, that have been here and have won so much here and can very clearly point the way of how to do it and the things that are the most important and undeniable.

"But then as well, [there is the] ambition from us that are here and still want to be here and keep on winning. They are joining and full of ambition and with all the dreams in the world. The mix of these makes it work."

Not only have there been major changes in the playing squad, but also in the dugout too, with Maresca replacing the legendary Pep Guardiola, who stepped down at the end of last season after 10 years in charge.

Maresca was previously assistant to the Spaniard at Etihad Stadium, before spells at Leicester City and Chelsea .

Dias said Guardiola's departure was not an "easy moment for the club", while Maresca was the "perfect person for the job" as he "knew the house so well".

City have started the season in perfect fashion, claiming four straight victories in the Premier League and Champions League, but face their sternest test so far with a trip to Manchester United on Sunday (kick-off 16:30 BST).

Asked how the Italian is doing things differently to his predecessor, Dias said: "There's obviously many things from training session to some details about the way we press, details about the way we defend and that make all of these Enzo's idea.

"I feel like everything is making a lot of sense. Everyone is buying into the idea. Everyone's excited about it and there is a lot of joy in training, which is massively important."

The speed of change at City means Dias is now one of the longest-serving players at the club.

The 29-year-old has played over 250 games, winning four Premier League titles, the Champions League and two FA Cups.

He is one of only four players remaining from the 2023 Treble-winning squad, alongside Erling Haaland, Phil Foden and Rico Lewis.

Last summer, Dias committed his future to the club by signing a contract extension until 2029, with the option of a further year.

He added: "I am 29, I am going to be 30 next year but I am excited about all of this and all the the things with the club, the new manager, new players, the new challenge, guys that I was so close with leaving.

"It's the circle of life, you can call it and it is just how things are. I am appreciative of all of it - I'm appreciative of the memories I have with all the ones that left and I'm excited with the memory about the memories I'm going to make with the ones that have just arrived.

"I am still very ambitious. I took the decision of being at this level because I feel like I have won so much but maybe the thing that would be my biggest reward would be to be here so many years playing at this level and and having the consistency of being ambitious for so long.

"I am excited. I think excited is the word."

articles.title: Anthony Gordon: How Barcelona's England winger hit ground running
articles.summary: Anthony Gordon's £70m move to Barcelona was questioned by some - but the England winger is already proving his worth for the free-scoring Spanish giants.
articles.body:
Anthony Gordon has only played five matches for Barcelona since joining in May, but the England winger is already making a big impression.

The former Newcastle United forward has provided four assists in his first five games for the free-scoring Spanish giants.

The 25-year-old is still hunting his first goal, but has slotted seamlessly into Barcelona's attack - in a left-wing spot often filled by on-loan England team-mate Marcus Rashford last term.

And Gordon is not just making an impression on the pitch.

He delivered his welcome speech in Spanish - a language he said he learned with the help of one of Newcastle's Spanish physios - before adding a couple of phrases in Catalan when speaking with fans.

While there were some questions over the decision to pay £70m for Gordon, it is easy to see why Barcelona's supporters are already chanting his name.

When Gordon completed his move this summer to become only the second English player to join Barcelona on a permanent deal, after Gary Lineker in 1986, there was plenty of curiosity surrounding the transfer.

It was a significant investment in a player who, despite an outstanding Champions League campaign, had been inconsistent in the Premier League and posted relatively modest numbers.

Newcastle finished 12th in the league, while Gordon managed six league goals and two assists in 26 appearances - with three goals coming from the penalty spot.

Naturally, that raised questions about whether he could slot straight into Barcelona's starting XI.

Just a few months earlier, Gordon had been given a glimpse of exactly what playing at the Nou Camp would feel like when Newcastle travelled to Barcelona for the second leg of their Champions League last-16 tie.

The Magpies were beaten 7-2 on the night - losing 8-3 on aggregate - but for Gordon, there was something significant about being in Barcelona and the occasion offered a taste of the stadium he would ultimately find himself calling home.

His European record also told a very different story to his domestic campaign.

Gordon netted 10 goals in 12 Champions League appearances, consistently raising his level against the best teams in Europe.

Only Real Madrid forward Kylian Mbappe (15) and Bayern Munich striker Harry Kane (14) scored more than Gordon in the Champions League last season.

The Englishman has hit the ground running in Spain and become an influential presence in Hansi Flick's Barcelona attack.

While he is still waiting for his first goal, Gordon's pace and directness are well suited to Barcelona's attack.

"Our idea of play is much more linked to Anthony's," Barcelona sporting director Deco replied when asked why they had chosen Gordon over Rashford.

"His style fits with what the coach is looking for."

And it seems Gordon has settled in very quickly.

"I feel at home already," Gordon said. "The city is amazing. The guys have made me feel so welcome. I think I will get better and better the longer I'm here."

Playing primarily from the left, he has given Flick another way of hurting opponents.

His ability to attack space stretches the defence, while his movement without the ball creates opportunities for team-mates.

That has been particularly noticeable alongside Lamine Yamal and Raphinha.

Barcelona boss Flick said: "I think as a striker, from his side, you want to score goals. He has had some chances and he missed them.

"But he has made the final pass to prepare the goals and this is also very important."

Gordon produced two assists in the space of four minutes against Elche in his debut league game.

He also went one-on-one with the Elche keeper and had the opportunity to score a debut goal.

However, Gordon instead chose to square the ball across the face of goal for Fermin Lopez, who made no mistake from close range.

That moment revealed plenty about Gordon's mentality to supporters. Rather than chasing the glory of a debut goal, he prioritised the better option for the team.

"You always want to win but it's always about the team first," Gordon said after the match. "Especially at this club."

For Barcelona supporters, it was another indication they had signed a player who is not simply interested in making an individual impact, but in doing whatever it takes to help the team succeed.

Flick's side have exploded out of the blocks this season, scoring 22 goals across their first five games while conceding only three.

It is the club's most prolific start since Flick took charge in May 2024.

Goals have come from all over the pitch, with Raphinha (eight) and Lamine Yamal (five) leading the way.

But Gordon's qualities have proved particularly valuable, with his ability to make aggressive runs and press from the front fitting naturally into Flick's system.

He can stay wide and isolate a full-back, attack the space behind a defence or drift inside and combine with Barcelona's other forwards.

And when the ball is lost, his willingness to immediately press helps Barcelona when they are out of possession.

It would be premature to suggest Gordon has answered every question after only a handful of games.

He is still waiting for his first goal, and maintaining this level of performance and intensity over an entire season will be a challenge.

But that is a very different conversation from the one surrounding him before his move.

Instead of asking whether he belongs at Barcelona, people are now discussing just how important he could become.

articles.title: Mbappe names Lamine Yamal among his favourite young players amid Ballon d’Or battle: ‘He’s got it all’
articles.summary: Kylian Mbappe has once again endorsed himself for the Ballon d’Or, stating that nobody enjoyed a better individual season than him, while also offering high...
articles.body:
Kylian Mbappe has once again endorsed himself for the Ballon d'Or, stating that nobody enjoyed a better individual season than him, while also offering high praise for Barcelona sensation Lamine Yamal.

The Real Madrid forward remains desperate to win the prestigious individual award for the first time, despite his second campaign at the Santiago Bernabeu failing to deliver the major team success he had hoped for.

Speaking to L'Equipe (h/t Mundo Deportivo ), Mbappe was unequivocal when asked about his Ballon d'Or credentials.

"Nobody had a better season last year than me," the French striker stated.

It is a bold claim, particularly with Yamal established among the leading contenders after a season in which the teenager combined spectacular numbers with a remarkable collection of honours.

Mbappe names Yamal among his favourite young stars

For what it is worth, Mbappe did not dismiss Yamal's challenge. Quite the opposite.

Mbappe has high praise for Lamine Yamal. (Photo by Yasser Bakhsh/Getty Images)

Asked about the young players he admires, the Real Madrid forward specifically singled out the Barcelona star, alongside a group of highly rated talents from across Europe.

"Among the young players, I like Lamine Yamal. He's got it all.

"I like Estevão – he's got a special creativity. Here, Arda Güler could go very far. Endrick has potential – he's a goalscorer. Warren (Zaïre-Emery) and Désiré (Doué) are bound to have great careers," he says.

Yamal's trophy haul strengthens his case

Yamal's Ballon d'Or argument is built around more than his individual brilliance.

The Barcelona forward has won the European Championship and World Cup with Spain, while also collecting the La Liga title and a Spanish Super Cup with Barcelona last season.

Lamine Yamal's case is also strong for Ballon d'Or debate. (Photo by Alex Caparros/Getty Images)

He now wears the captain's armband for Barça , which is another indication of how quickly his status has risen.

Mbappe, by contrast, produced an outstanding individual campaign but Real Madrid did not turn his goals and performances into the major trophies expected at the Bernabéu.

The Ballon d'Or debate has a clear tension

That leaves the central question of this year's race: should extraordinary individual output outweigh collective success?

Mbappe believes his own performances deserve the award. Barcelona's hierarchy, including Hansi Flick and Deco, sees the case for Yamal differently .

At present, the Ballon d'Or contest looks increasingly like a battle between two players representing very different cases – Mbappe's individual dominance against Yamal's combination of performance, silverware and influence.

articles.title: The fine Real Madrid have imposed on Raul Asencio after disciplinary case – report
articles.summary: Real Madrid defender Raul Asencio found himself in controversy after being involved in a drunk-driving incident.Los Blancos have now imposed a substantial fi...
articles.body:
Real Madrid defender Raul Asencio found himself in controversy after being involved in a drunk-driving incident.

Los Blancos have now imposed a substantial financial penalty on the Spaniard following the disciplinary proceedings opened against the defender.

According to Defensa Central , the sanction is believed to be close to €100,000. Analyst Rodra has revealed that Asencio has already received punishment from Madrid.

The reported punishment is approaching €100,000, although it remains unclear whether Madrid now consider the disciplinary process completely closed.

The club's frustration is also said to go beyond this particular incident. There is concern internally about an accumulation of problems involving Asencio.

However, Madrid do not consider what happened to be something that should end the defender's career.

Raul Asencio is going through a difficult time in his career. (Photo by Angel Martinez/Getty Images)

Similar off-field mistakes have happened with players at Madrid and elsewhere, but the club nevertheless considered this case serious enough to warrant a major financial sanction.

Asencio's situation was already complicated before the disciplinary issue.

Jose Mourinho did not initially count on the defender when he returned to Madrid and requested another centre-back.

Asencio ultimately remained at the club and managed to change some of Mourinho's thinking through his commitment and work in training.

Competition remains extremely difficult, however.

Ibrahima Konate and Dean Huijsen have established themselves as the preferred centre-back partnership early in the season, while Antonio Rudiger is another option and Eder Militao is working towards his return.

Asencio has difficult job of rebuilding trust

Asencio needs to rebuild his trust at Madrid. (Photo by Angel Martinez/Getty Images)

Asencio has put his foot in the mud, but Madrid are willing to give him another chance.

The financial punishment sends a clear message about the standards Madrid expect away from the pitch and sets a template for other players in the squad.

For Asencio, the response now has to come through professionalism.

He needs to recover from injury, return to training , remain disciplined and take whatever opportunities Mourinho gives him. Breaking into Madrid's defensive rotation was already going to be difficult.

After this episode, proving he can be trusted both on and off the pitch has become just as important as proving his quality as a defender.

articles.title: Johnson lassos Odessa in weather shortened game
articles.summary: Led by senior quarterback Elvis Estrada and a stout defense, Johnson rolled up 28 points on its way to a 37-0 win over Odessa in a game that was called off a...
articles.body:
Johnson needed to show up for only one half to defeat Odessa on Friday at Heroes Stadium.

Led by Jaguars senior quarterback Elvis Estrada and a stout defense, Johnson (2-0), ranked No. 1 by the Express-News and No. 6 in the Class 6A poll, rolled up 28 points in the second quarter on its way to a 37-0 win over Odessa in a game that was called off after halftime due to severe weather.

It was the second time this season severe weather shortened a game Johnson was playing in. Its season opener two weeks ago against Judson, also played at Heroes Stadium, was canceled in the middle of the first quarter after a storm knocked out power to the stadium.

Unlike its season opener, Johnson was able to get in one full half of play and it made good use of it, with Estrada passing for an efficient 12-of-15 passing for 190 yards and one score, and the defensive unit shut down Odessa (2-1), holding the Bronchos to 36 total yards.

Even though Johnson had a commanding lead at halftime, Johnson coach TP Miller pointed out the early mistakes his team made on two of its early drives in the first half, a bad snap which ruined a field goal attempt and a fumble in the red zone which stopped a potential scoring drive.

"We had some stern talking during the halftime about the self-inflicted wounds we did and uncharacteristic mistakes first half," Miller said. "With that, it was a growth moment, it was a learning moment coming from a big win last week (a 38-7 win over Austin Vandegrift) and then going into this game. So, we just got to be patient and continue to strive to do better every week."

Johnson got off to an uneven start, as two of its first three drives ended in mistakes, a bad snap that ruined a field goal attempt and a fumble in the red zone. In between those ill-fated drives, Noah Cartright scored on an 11-yard run with 3:45 in the first quarter for a 7-0 Johnson lead.

The Jaguars picked up a safety late in the opening quarter when Matthew Paris sacked Odessa quarterback Phillip Carrasco in the end zone, extending Johnson's lead to 9-0. It was one of two sacks for Paris in the game.

Johnson started rolling in the second quarter, with Jeremiah Johnson scoring on a 14-yard run on the first play of the frame. Then the Jaguars' special teams came up with two scores, on a thrilling 68-yard punt return from Braelyn Allen and 31-yard return from Eli McNeil off a blocked punt. Allen scored one more time on a 50-yard scoring pass from Estrada, with 1:17 left in the first half, before the storm rolled in at halftime.

"The game has slowed down for Elvis (Estrada)," Miller said. "I think it's credit to his hard work. Starting off as a sophomore and then as a junior, I think under his belt I think we've only lost two or three games, compared to our 20 wins as well. It's just experience. He's doing a heck of a job leading the offense and credit to his offensive line and running backs and everybody else. It's really a group effort."

With its dominance for one half over Odessa, Miller said the Johnson defensive unit has shown improvement every week.

"I love how they're running to the ball," Miller said. "Every week our tackling is getting better. But one thing that we have learned is we're an aggressive defense. We're going to apply pressure and we're going to cover well and make plays. So, I really love how (defensive coordinator Michael Mull) and our coaching staff and our players have really grown into this style of defense."

Players from both teams had just come out onto the field after halftime before game officials decided to suspend the game because of lightning. After an hour delay, the game was called off with Johnson being awarded the win.

Johnson has an upcoming bye week, which will give it time to rest up and watch game film on its next opponent, a LEE squad which is off to a surprising 3-0 start after a 16-3 win over MacArthur on Thursday. Johnson and LEE kick off District 28-6A action on Sept. 24 at Comalander Stadium.

articles.title: NFL Week 1 Sunday Night Football— Ferguson And Dart Player Props
articles.summary: Check out which player for the Dallas Cowboys has an appealing under for receiving yards and which one on the New York Giants has an eye-catching over for ru...
articles.body:
The NFC East is in the spotlight on Sunday Night Football in Week 1. The New York Giants are hosting the Dallas Cowboys . The visitors are 3.0-point favorites in New Jersey. The spread is slight, but it matters for the expected game script, which is critical to play-calling projections.

The favored Cowboys might not need to air it out from start to finish. Meanwhile, the underdog Giants might need to drop back more often to keep up or catch up. While the expected game script was considered, it wasn't the only factor behind the following two player props: an under on receiving yards for a tertiary pass-catching option on the Cowboys, and an over on Big Blue's dual-threat quarterback.

NFL Week 1: Sunday Night Football Player Props

Jake Ferguson Under 30.5 Receiving Yards (-115) at DraftKings Sportsbook

Jaxson Dart Over 30.5 Rushing Yards (-110) at BetMGM

Jake Ferguson was a reliable pass-catching option for Dak Prescott and the Cowboys last year, logging 102 targets, 82 receptions (4.8 per game), 600 receiving yards (35.3 per game) and eight touchdown receptions. He also had only 7.3 yards per reception, a career low, and 5.9 yards per target, the second-lowest-mark in his career, behind only his 5.7 yards per target in 2025.

Ferguson isn't a dynamic or efficient receiver. Furthermore, his overall numbers are inflated by the time CeeDee Lamb was limited or missed last year. Ferguson played 13 games when Lamb played at least 20 snaps and four when Lamb fell short of that threshold.

In the four games that Lamb fell short of 20 snaps, Ferguson had a 68.4% route participation rate, 22.3% target share, 0.31 targets per route run (TPRR), 7.5 receptions per game, 51.0 receiving yards per game and 1.92 yards per route run (Y/RR).

In the 13 games when Lamb played at least 20 snaps, Ferguson had a 69.8% route participation rate, 14.1% target share, 0.18 TPRR, 4.0 receptions per game, 30.5 receiving yards per game and 1.07 Y/RR.

As the splits demonstrate, Ferguson was much less involved and efficient when he was bumped down the pecking order behind Lamb and George Pickens . Ryan Flournoy is also a roadblock to Ferguson's receiving opportunities, and the Cowboys thought enough of the young wide receiver to sign him to a one-year contract extension on Friday.

The Cowboys likely won't need much from their steady-but-unspectacular tight end on Sunday night. After failing to clear even 20 receiving yards in his last four games played in 2025 , Ferguson should come up short of 30.5 receiving yards on Sunday Night Football in Week 1.

Jaxson Dart teased his potential last season, which included giving the opposition trouble with his legs. As a rookie, Dart averaged 7.0 rush attempts and 40.6 rushing yards per game in his 12 starts.

He was used at times as a designed runner, but he was also lethal as a scrambler. Dart's 290 scramble yards were the ninth most among quarterbacks last year. Conversely, the Cowboys were tied for the third-most scramble yards allowed per game in 2025 at 19.3. With designed runs factored in, Dallas allowed 23.4 rushing yards per game to opposing quarterbacks in 2025, and many weren't the caliber of runner Dart was.

Dart has a favorable matchup to showcase his rushing ability. He might also be called on to drop back often because the Giants are underdogs, but also because of the play-calling tendencies against the Cowboys after they acquired stud defensive lineman Quinnen Williams last year.

The league average for pass rate over expected (PROE) last year in the regular season was 0.4%. In Dallas's first 10 games of the year, before they acquired Williams, they faced a 1.6% PROE. That mark surged to an 8.4% PROE in the seven games Williams suited up for the Cowboys.

Furthermore, the Cowboys faced a 57.8% pass rate on snaps when Williams was off the field and a 69.7% pass rate on snaps when he was on the field. Dart could have his number called on a designed rush or two on Sunday Night Football, but his scrambling ability and the likelihood of him dropping back often fuel the appeal of his player prop for over 30.5 rushing yards.

articles.title: "Vamos a pedir no jugar aquí"
articles.standfirst: Felines, que debutó en LaLiga como entrenador del Rayo en el Bernabéu, se frustró ante la cadena de goleadas en Chamartín
articles.summary: Felines, que debutó en LaLiga como entrenador del Rayo en el Bernabéu, se frustró ante la cadena de goleadas en Chamartín
articles.body: El Rayo Vallecano se presentó en Primera en la temporada 1977-78. El equipo de la franja se ganó pronto el apodo de matagigantes, una leyenda que comenzó a forjarse cuando el 30 de octubre derrotó al Madrid por 3-2 con el gol de Landaburu al final. En la campaña de su estreno en la élite, en Vallecas cayeron los seis primeros al final de la Liga (Madrid, Barcelona, Athletic, Valencia, Sporting y Atlético de Madrid) y sólo ganó el Elche (0-1). Fueron tres temporadas consecutivas en Primera en las que el Rayo mostraba una cara muy distinta en casa que fuera. Pero hubo un estadio en el que nunca fue capaz de poner en problemas al equipo de casa y regresó a la barriada con una goleada en la mochila: el Santiago Bernabéu. A Chamartín llega ahora el Rayo con cuatro derrotas mínimas y un empate en sus últimas cinco campañas. Son la otra cara de una presentación en la casa del Madrid en la que en tres partidos encajó 16 goles y marcó tres. En ese clima de alta tensión, el Rayo fichó a Rafa Iriondo, un técnico campeón de Copa con el Athletic y el Betis. Eso fue el 31 de enero, el mismo día que el Rayo se enfrentaba al Espanyol en Copa. Ganó 2-0 en la ida de los cuartos y con Felines en su banquillo. Era el debut de la leyenda del Rayo como entrenador de su equipo. Con el tiempo encima y el acuerdo con Iriondo fijado para que empezara a entrenar el lunes, la visita al dentista en Chamartín quedaba al mando de Felines. “Era algo que ya esperaba. La verdad es que, como rayista que soy, me debo al club y acepto las decisiones de los que mandan con disciplina. “Tanto Peñalva como yo sabíamos que nuestra posición al frente del equipo era temporal. Lo que hace falta es que, con la llegada de Iriondo, todo se arregle, y juntos llevemos al Rayo al lugar que le corresponde”, comentaba Felines el día de antes del partido con el Madrid. Con la boca pequeña explicaba que podían dar un disgusto al Madrid. Los blancos eran segundos, pero venían de dos derrotas seguidas en Liga: San Mamés y Mestalla. Su alivio era que la Real, líder, había desperdiciado con dos empates (Atlético de Madrid y Las Palmas) la oportunidad de abrir brecha. Esa Liga se decidió por un punto a favor del Madrid y con sólo una derrota de la Real: ante el Sevilla en la penúltima jornada. Esa campaña acabó con doblete blanco en la famosa final de Copa ante su fililal, el Castilla (6-1). La crítica en el Madrid se centraba en los delanteros. A cero se habían quedado los de Boskov ante el Athletic (3-0) y Valencia (0-0). De ese duelo de dudas salió perdiendo el más débil. Pura lógica. El Rayo, que ya llevaba la herida mortal del descenso en su cuerpo, fue presa fácil para el Madrid. La crisis de los delanteros blancos encontró en las fatigas rayistas una cura perfecta. A los diez minutos de partido ya habían marcado dos de los tres delanteros que mandó Boskov al campo: Santillana y Juanito. Antes de los veinte llegó el gol del tercero, con la firma de Laurie Cunningham. De nada alivió al equipo de Felines que el jugador del Madrid más en forma, Juanito, se lesionara al llegar al cuarto de hora. El partido acabó en una paliza, con siete goles en el marcador blanco y ninguno en el del Rayo. Santillana, que no veía puerta desde el 16 de diciembre, firmó dos y entró en una racha en la que anotaría 17 más. A la jornada siguiente, el Madrid daría un golpe de autoridad en la Liga al ganar 0-2 en la casa de un Barcelona que deambulaba por la zona media-baja de la clasificación. La sensación de satisfacción por la goleada en el vestuario del Madrid no tapaba que el rival apenas había ofrecido resistencia. “Quizá el Rayo haya dado facilidades. Ha intentado jugar con alegría y nuestros primeros goles le han desmoralizado”, aseguraba Juanito. Felines era mucho más contundente al analizar un 7-0 que se sumaba a las dos claras derrotas del Rayo en sus primeras visitas a Chamartín: 5-2 y 4-1. “Hay que decir en la Federación que nos quiten estos partidos con el Madrid, pedir no jugar más aquí. Llevo tres años viendo al Rayo aquí y siempre ocurre igual. Los jugadores salen acomplejados, con miedo, sin ideas. Parece como si nunca se hubieran calzado las botas. No creo que el Madrid se encuentre con otro chollo como éste. Venimos aquí y parecemos un equipo de seda”, comentaba apesadumbrado. El entrenador era una voz más dentro de un vestuario con un mensaje común: “Todo lo hemos hecho mal”. El Rayo no volvió a Primera hasta la temporada 1989-90. Perdió con el Madrid de Toshack. Por 5-2 El 7-0 de 1980 pasó a la historia el 20 de diciembre de 2015. Ese día, el Madrid de ganó al Rayo por 10-2.

articles.title: Real Madrid star Kylian Mbappe backs himself for Ballon d’ Or and responds to viral ‘dictator’ nickname
articles.summary: Real Madrid are preparing to face Rayo Vallecano in La Liga, and Kylian Mbappe will be hoping to continue his good start to the season.The Frenchman has scor...
articles.body:
Real Madrid are preparing to face Rayo Vallecano in La Liga , and Kylian Mbappe will be hoping to continue his good start to the season.

The Frenchman has scored five goals in five games across all competitions so far. He has insisted that his goalscoring will never be a problem despite the criticism levelled at him.

As quoted by Mundo Deportivo , Mbappe has spoken openly about two very different subjects surrounding him at Madrid: his viral "dictator" nickname and his ambition to finally win the Ballon d'Or.

The nickname originated from a joke made by Ousmane Dembele during a France camp, and Mbappe drew a clear distinction between that and some of the harsher narratives circulating online.

"Sometimes it shows a lack of political and human awareness," Mbappe said.

On Dembele's version of the joke, however, his tone was much lighter.

"What Ousmane does is different. He got it from social media! His version is something to laugh about, not something meant to hurt," Mbappe explained.

The important point for Madrid is that Mbappe does not appear distracted by the noise surrounding him.

He is comfortable enough to joke about part of it while still setting boundaries where he feels they are needed.

Mbappe was even more direct when the subject turned to the Ballon d'Or.

"Who would I vote for? Myself," he said with a laugh.

"I have the idea that I can win it this year, so I have not taken a step back on that subject. Of course I can win it.

" I have arguments, like being the all-time leading scorer in World Cup history ahead of great legends, in the biggest tournament ever created," he continued.

Mbappe has never hidden his individual ambition, and there is no reason he should. At Madrid, the challenge is simply making sure personal goals remain tied to collective success.

Mbappe believes he deserves the Ballon d'Or this year. (Photo by Denis Doyle/Getty Images)

Mbappe also pointed out that individual awards are always subjective.

"Or being the top scorer in other competitions alongside other great players. It is an individual award, and there has never been unanimity over the winners, so many people think they can win it," the Frenchman concluded.

Mbappe had an excellent club season with Madrid despite the team overall failing to win any silverware.

He then continued his excellent form at the World Cup, where he walked away with the Golden Boot ahead of the likes of Lionel Messi .

There is a case to be made for Mbappe to be the deserving Ballon d'Or winner this season, and it remains to be seen how matters unfold.

articles.title: Manuel Neuer becomes the oldest German player in UCL history
articles.summary: Unc still got it.
articles.body:
Manuel Neuer is one of, if not, the greatest goalkeeper of all time. While he hasn't been the subject of much praise in recent months, we now have an opportunity to come and celebrate the legendary goalkeeper. This week after his start against Bodø/Glimt, Neuer became the oldest German player in the history of the Champions League.

He has now surpassed legendary German Jens Lehmann, who also played as a goalkeeper. It does seem to be goalkeepers breaking these records, but that doesn't take anything away from this accomplishment. Neuer's longevity is simply brilliant, no matter how much his performances have cooled down over the years.

While it is an opportunity to celebrate, some fans might take the opportunity to look at this a bit more skeptically. Is this an amazing accomplishment? Yes, but perhaps a world-class squad such as Bayern Munich should aim to have a different choice in goal, considering the club's starting goalkeeper is now over 40 years old.

Looking at other top clubs such as Real Madrid , Arsenal , and PSG , Neuer's age certainly does stand out in comparison to these club's goalkeepers. Food for thought.

articles.title: Lauren Hemp: Manchester City forward has a legacy at 26
articles.summary: Manchester City forward Lauren Hemp has already achieved more than most footballers at the age of 26.
articles.body:
Lauren Hemp has already achieved more than most footballers at the age of 26.

The England international made her 200th appearance for Manchester City last Sunday as they began the defence of their Women's Super League title.

She was player of the match as they beat newly promoted Birmingham City 3-1, capping off her milestone appearance in the perfect way.

Hemp is only the fourth player in City's history to reach the landmark of 200 appearances, following Steph Houghton, Keira Walsh and Demi Stokes.

During her eight years at the club, she has grown to become one of Europe's best forwards and helped them lift six major trophies.

It was no surprise City manager Andree Jeglertz said Hemp "already has a legacy" - and there is still plenty of time to build on it.

Find interviews and extra content on the BBC Women's Football Weekly feed

New contenders emerge on WSL return - but Man City start strong

Individual accolades have flooded in during Hemp's time at City.

She scooped up a record fourth Professional Footballers' Association young player of the year award in 2022, has been named in the PFA team of the year three times and has established herself as a key member of Sarina Wiegman's Lionesses.

Hemp has netted 74 goals in 200 appearances and has created more chances from open play than any other player in the WSL's history.

Only striker Khadija Shaw has scored more City goals in the professional era than Hemp, and the England forward is second in the WSL's all-time assist charts.

Against Birmingham, she had more entries in the final third than any team-mate besides Gracie Prior and 16 touches in the opposition box.

In summary, Hemp has proved to be a crucial player for City and starred as they won a domestic double under Jeglertz last season.

"Just give her the ball and something happens!" he said after the victory over Birmingham.

"What I feel is fascinating with Lauren is that if you come and watch one of our training sessions, you see she has the same enjoyment for playing football that she shows in games.

"I really hope she never loses that. She is always kicking a ball, she is never too tired to do anything and she wants to be there. She loves football.

"That shows young players what it's about. They need to love to go to work. It's not just a job, it's an identity.

"What she has done for the club in 200 games... she is still pretty young. She can play many more games here. That's amazing that she has a legacy already."

Hemp's City career has also coincided with a successful period for the Lionesses in which she played a key role in helping them win back-to-back European titles.

Having joined from Bristol City as a high-flying teenager in 2018, she has grown up during her time in Manchester.

She was awarded an MBE in 2024 for services to football, and signed a three-year contract extension with City that year.

Last season the club won their first WSL title in a decade, as well as the Women's FA Cup - reward for Hemp's commitment.

Jayne Comer, secretary for the Manchester City supporters club and a season ticket holder for more than 10 years, said Hemp was already considered a "legend".

"She is absolutely loved by us all. She remained fiercely loyal to the club, when, let's face it, she could have signed for any team in the world," Comer told BBC Sport.

"The fact she stayed and gives her all every week means so much to us. We've had the privilege of watching one of the best players in the world.

"Every week she gets us all on our feet. When she gets the ball, it's exciting. You always feel like something spectacular might happen."

Comer, who watched Hemp play live before she joined City, also considered her "one of the greatest players we've ever had".

"She is always one of the first names on the teamsheet for any manager and looks like somebody who loves to play football," she added.

"I remember the very first time I saw Lauren play was when we were away at Bristol and she really caught my attention.

"Even back then, you could see what a talent she was. She just oozed potential. I was really excited to see how she would progress and I have not been disappointed.

"What a player! I count myself lucky every time I see her playing in sky blue."

City visit Aston Villa in the WSL on Sunday (18:30 BST).

articles.title: Nueve años de cárcel al líder del secuestro de Donnarumma y su mujer
articles.summary: Ilyas Kherbouch, 21 años y apodado 'Ganito', ha sido condenado a nueve años de cárcel y 80.000 euros de multa por haber encabezado el violento secuestro en julio de 2023 del portero internacional italiano Gianluigi Donnarumma, entonces en el PSG, y de su pareja, quien estaba embarazada y sufrió un aborto espontáneo poco tiempo después.
articles.body: Ilyas Kherbouch, 21 años y apodado 'Ganito', ha sido condenado a nueve años de cárcel y 80.000 euros de multa por haber encabezado el violento secuestro en julio de 2023 del portero internacional italiano Gianluigi Donnarumma, entonces en el PSG, y de su pareja, quien estaba embarazada y sufrió un aborto espontáneo poco tiempo después. En una sentencia divulgada en la madrugada de este sábado, tras un proceso que se celebró el 10 y el 11 de septiembre en el Tribunal Correccional de París y que tuvo que ser interrumpido por insultos y amenazas de 'Ganito', su colega Khyan Mamouni, 22 años y designado por la acusación como el otro cerebro de la operación, fue absuelto. Otro de los participantes, Moktar Diop, 24 años, ha sido condenado a cinco años de cárcel, dos exentos de cumplimiento. El actual portero del Manchester City y su pareja, Alessia Elefante, no asistieron al juicio. El asalto y secuestro a la casa del meta italiano en el lujoso distrito VIII de París fue de una especial violencia, pues ambos llegaron a ser maniatados y golpeados. Elefante estaba embarazada de sólo unas semanas y, poco después del incidente, perdió al feto en un aborto espontáneo. El botín estimado que se llevaron los asaltantes fue en torno a un millón de euros.

articles.title: Esperando a Bernardo
articles.standfirst: Mou suspira por la mejor versión del medio, llamado a ser clave en una zona de creación necesitada de su talento
articles.summary: Mou suspira por la mejor versión del medio, llamado a ser clave en una zona de creación necesitada de su talento
articles.body: El partido del martes ante el Inter de Milán evidenció la que para muchos es la gran carencia del nuevo Real Madrid. La falta de control en el centro del campo convirtió el partido en una gincana de la que los blancos salieron vivos porque Courtois volvió a estar en modo pulpo. Cierto es que también los delanteros blancos perdonaron, y mucho, pero el partido no fue bien gestionado por el Madrid en casi ningún momento. Y eso generó inquietud, y algunos pitos, en un Bernabéu que no acaba de ver solución a los males que vienen aquejando al equipo en los dos últimos años. José Mourinho cree tener la solución. Ésta pasa por las botas de Bernardo Silva, que se perdió el partido de Champions por sanción, al igual que Arda y Camavinga. Tres bajas que dejaron la medular en paños menores, una situación que Mou quiso salvar adelantando a Trent para ayudar a Fede en las tareas de creación. No salió bien, por lo que, salvo en casos de extrema necesidad (el partido del martes lo fue) no se debería volver a repetir. La no llegada de Rodri fue un golpe para el Madrid, pero el club y Mourinho creyeron tener el problema resuelto, al menos en parte, tras lograr con anterioridad a ese episodio el sí de Bernardo Silva, la manija del gran City de Guardiola. El club blanco se impuso en una carrera en la que también participaron Barça y Atlético de Madrid, entre otros, por los servicios de un jugador que llegaba libre y con una edad razonable (32 años cumplidos el pasado 10 de agosto). La llamada de Mou fue decisiva para que Silva se decantara por el Madrid, pero lo cierto es que, hasta el momento, el peso del luso en el equipo ha sido limitado. El propio entrenador le afeó en público no haberse 'matado' físicamente en verano, lo que puede explicar unos números de momento discretos: sólo 205 minutos repartidos en cuatro partidos, con dos titularidades, en los dos primeros partidos del curso. Lo cierto es que las mejores sensaciones de Bernardo llegaron en la pretemporada, en la que sí destacó como nuevo metrónomo de un equipo aún en plena fase de rodaje. Más o menos como sigue ahora, plasmando aún la idea de Mou y con Bernardo apareciendo poco más de media hora en los tres últimos partidos. El portugués, que viene de jugar 53 partidos la temporada pasada con el City, es esperado como agua de mayo por Mou, que no contempla (al menos de momento) la posibilidad de retrasar a Arda Güler a la base. Para el técnico del Madrid, el turco es mejor cuanto más cerca del área esté, aunque lo ve en el futuro jugando más atrás. No ahora, porque Güler ha demostrado ser el futbolista de la plantilla con más capacidad de aclarar jugadas en zona de tres cuartos. Para sacar el balón jugado Mou cuenta con un Bernardo que debe ir ganando físico para coger galones en la zona de creación, ya que Valverde, Camavinga o Tchouaméni son futbolistas de un perfil menos creativo.

articles.title: Barrios se cae
articles.standfirst: El centrocampista sufre una lesión en el sóleo que le hará perderse los próximos partidos. El derbi, casi imposible
articles.summary: El centrocampista sufre una lesión en el sóleo que le hará perderse los próximos partidos. El derbi, casi imposible
articles.body: Lo que el pasado miércoles, cuando era sustituido en Anfield en la segunda parte (abandonaría el verde en el minuto 77) encendía las alarmas, ha acabado por convertirse en la peor noticia posible: Barrios está lesionado. El mejor jugador del Atlético tendrá que parar como consecuencia de una lesión en el sóleo. Concretamente, tiene una afectación miofascial de bajo grado, que si bien no reviste mucha gravedad, sí es lo suficiente como para que se pierda los próximos partidos. Ni más ni menos que los tres encuentros de la próxima semana. Barrios no estará este domingo en Anoeta, ni el miércoles para recibir a Osasuna ni, muy probablemente, en el derbi frente al Real Madrid. En este sentido, los plazos para que pudiera estar en la gran cita son muy justos, con lo que todo apunta a que no volverá hasta después del parón. Un duro golpe en la línea de flotación del Atlético, que ahora deberá hacer frente a una semana de máxima intensidad sin la presencia de su jugador bandera. En este sentido, y más aún teniendo en cuenta que la temporada pasada tuvo que afrontar el tramo decisivo del curso sin el centrocampista, no se forzará su recuperación en absoluto.
